messages.author: 1961bafd93e11caa
messages.subject: Invisible linetypes in in pdf
parts:
Hi all,

I'm having a weird problem with linetypes. When I plot data with five
lines (different linetypes), and plot it to pdf, one of the linetypes
is somehow invisible, e.g.:

dat = data.frame(a=1:100,b=rep(1:5,each = 20))

pdf('test2.pdf',width=7,height=4)
ggplot(data=dat) + geom_line(aes(1:20,a,linetype=factor(b)))
dev.off()

the fifth linetype is invisible in the pdf (but not on the screen with
quartz). I also tried the following variations:

(1) + scale_linetype_manual(values = c(1,2,3,4,5))
(2) + scale_linetype_manual(values = c(1,2,3,4,6))
(3) + scale_linetype_manual(values = c(6,7,8,9,10))

Surprisingly, the linetypes are not even consistent (i.e., in (1) and
(2) the first 4 lines do not have the same type in the plot), but also
with any of these options there is *always* one of the five lines that
is invisible...

does anyone have a clue how to solve this weird issue?

Thank you very much!
Michel

messages.author: fc22cb727156ff4f
messages.subject: Re: Invisible linetypes in in pdf
parts:
On Mon, Dec 7, 2009 at 13:08, Michel <michel.m...@gmail.com> wrote:
> does anyone have a clue how to solve this weird issue?

that's a bug in the pdf() device of R I think. It has come up quite a
few times on this list already. try using quartz(type="pdf") instead.

JiHO
---
http://maururu.net

messages.author: fc22cb727156ff4f
messages.subject: Re: Invisible linetypes in in pdf
parts:
Remember to reply all so that other people on the list can see your posts.

On Mon, Dec 7, 2009 at 15:19, Michel Meulpolder
<michel.m...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the answer. However, when I try quartz(type="pdf") with a dataset
> of many points, I get linetypes show inconsistent behavior (i.e., some parts
> of dotted lines become continuous). My hypothesis is that quartz/ggplot
> connects every two succeeding points with a 'new' line, and therefore points
> too close together do not exhibit a clear line pattern.

well, that's very strange. Does it also look like that on screen when
you plot it? I thought quartz() was pretty immune to this. What you
could do is:
- try ggsave but I am afraid it won't do better
- try copying from the screen (select your plot window and hit ⌘C)
then paste into preview (in Preview: File > New from Clipboard). This
creates a PDF which should be exactly what you have on screen. Un
fortunately it is not automated
- install Cairo and try the CairoPDF device

JiHO
---
http://maururu.net

I can confirm the pdf problem (even with R-dev), but quartz() works
for me. Could you post a minimal example where you see "inconsistent
behavior"?

a = 1:10000
ggplot() + geom_line(aes(a,a,linetype="a")) + geom_line(aes(a,1000 + a*2,linetype="b")) + scale_x_log10()

Thanks,
Michel

Yet another option is the tikzDevice package, which produces a pdf
through latex.

HTH,

parts:
Hi,

if you do send a bug report you might want to make it clear that it's
not related to ggplot2 by providing a raw Grid example,

x = seq(0, 10, length=10000)
y = cos(x)

pdf("test-pdf.pdf", width=4, height=4)
pushViewport(viewport(xscale=c(0, 10), yscale=c(0, 6)))
for(ind in 1:5)
grid.lines(x, y+ind, gp=gpar(lty=ind), default.units="native")
dev.off()

quartz(type="pdf", file="test-quartz.pdf", width=4, height=4)
pushViewport(viewport(xscale=c(0, 10), yscale=c(0, 6)))
for(ind in 1:5)
grid.lines(x, y+ind, gp=gpar(lty=ind), default.units="native")
dev.off()


The algorithm that computes the dashed lines is clearly working better
for pdf than for quartz when the points are very dense.

I can't reproduce the disappearance of the lines in the pdf device
though, I'm wondering if it's not a ggplot2 bug?

Best,

baptiste

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Invisible linetypes in in pdf
parts:
Regarding the original bug (invisible lines for pdf), does anyone know
if it has been reported to the R team?

I think I nailed the problem to an unfortunate side-effect of lineend="butt",

pdf("test.pdf")
grid.newpage()
grid.lines(gp=gpar(lty="13"))
grid.newpage()
grid.lines(gp=gpar(lty="13", lineend = "butt"))
dev.off()

Illustrator recognises a line in both pages in the pdf output, however
in the second page the line pattern has zero solid length because of
the lineend.

It may be that this is the correct behavior and that quartz() actually
cheats, I don't know. From the perspective of ggplot2, it might good
to change the lineend parameter in geom_path ?


Best,

baptiste

parts:
Hi all,

I'm not familiar with the process of reporting bugs to R core.
PR#14128 seems quite serious to me yet no-one replied publicly to the
report and for all I know it might end up forgotten in the long list
of pending reports.

Would it help if someone else joined the discussion on R-devel and
confirmed that this is indeed a serious problem with pdf output? It's
especially important to us ggplot2 users that we face the total
disappearance of a particular linetype; such an issue is less obvious
with other graphics packages that do not use the same lineend ("butt")
by default. I think consistency across devices should be more
important than the back-compatibility issue.


Thanks,

baptiste
